docs.title: Home
docs.text:
DoctrineDiagramBundle is a Symfony bundle that generates ER and Class diagrams representing the current state of your database.

This bundle is not intended as a design tool but rather as a utility for monitoring and visualizing database schema status.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Generate Entity-Relationship and UML Class diagrams from your Doctrine schema.
  • Choose the level of detail: mini, midi, or maxi.
  • Export diagrams as puml, svg, or png.
  • Style diagrams with built-in PlantUML themes.
  • Filter the entities or tables that appear in a diagram.
  • Convert PlantUML output locally (jar) or via a remote server.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Install the bundle
  2. Generating diagrams
  3. Configure the bundle

For conversion setup, see PlantUML setup. If generation fails, check the known issues.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• PHP 8.2+
  • Symfony 7.x or 8.x
  • PlantUML (only needed for png / svg output)

docs.title: How to configure the bundle
docs.text:
There are two ways to configure DoctrineDiagramBundle.

  1. Using a configuration file config/packages/doctrine_diagram.yaml.
  2. Using command's options.

Info

Command line options will always have priority over configuration file.

docs.title: Command's options
docs.text:
Use help command to see available options for doctrine:diagram:er and doctrine:diagram:class.

$ bin/console help doctrine:diagram:er
Description:
  Create an Entity-Relationship diagram.

Usage:
  doctrine:diagram:er [options]

Options:
      --filename=FILENAME      Destination file name.
      --format=FORMAT          Diagram format (svg, png or puml).
      --size=SIZE              Diagram size (mini, midi or maxi).
      --converter=CONVERTER    Which strategy will be used to convert puml to another format (auto, jar or server).
      --server=SERVER          PlantUML server URL, used to convert puml diagrams to svg or png.
      --jar=JAR                Path to plantuml.jar, used to convert puml diagrams to svg or png.
      --connection=CONNECTION  Doctrine connection to use.
      --theme=THEME            Theme name, this will change colors and style.
      --include=INCLUDE        Name of the table to include in the diagram. (multiple values allowed)
      --exclude=EXCLUDE        Name of the table to exclude from the diagram. (multiple values allowed)

$ bin/console help doctrine:diagram:class
Description:
  Create a Class diagram.

Usage:
  doctrine:diagram:class [options]

Options:
      --filename=FILENAME    Destination file name.
      --format=FORMAT        Diagram format (svg, png or puml).
      --size=SIZE            Diagram size (mini, midi or maxi).
      --converter=CONVERTER  Which strategy will be used to convert puml to another format (auto, jar or server).
      --server=SERVER        PlantUML server URL, used to convert puml diagrams to svg or png.
      --jar=JAR              Path to plantuml.jar, used to convert puml diagrams to svg or png.
      --em=EM                Entity Manager to use.
      --theme=THEME          Theme name, this will change colors and style.
      --include=INCLUDE      Name of the class to include in the diagram. (multiple values allowed)
      --exclude=EXCLUDE      Name of the class to exclude from the diagram. (multiple values allowed)

Tip

The commands doctrine:diagram:er and doctrine:diagram:class share almost all the same options, the only difference is that doctrine:diagram:er uses the --connection option, while doctrine:diagram:class uses --em.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Configuration file is located at config/packages/doctrine_diagram.yaml, this is a full configuration example:

doctrine_diagram:
    er:
        filename: '%kernel.project_dir%/er'
        size: midi
        theme: crt-amber
        connection: ~
        include:
            - table1
            - table2
        exclude:
            - table3
            - table4
    class:
        filename: '%kernel.project_dir%/class'
        size: mini
        theme: plain
        em: ~
        include:
            - App\Entity\Client
            - App\Entity\Feeback
        exclude:
            - App\Entity\User
            - App\Entity\CreditCard
    convert:
        format: svg
        converter: auto
        jar: /usr/bin/plantuml
        server: 'http://www.plantuml.com/plantuml'

Use the following commands to see your current configuration and all available options:

bin/console debug:config doctrine_diagram
bin/console config:dump-reference doctrine_diagram

docs.title: Specify diagram name
docs.text:
By default, the diagram filename is er.svg for Entity-Relationship diagrams and class.svg for Class diagrams. The file extension is added automatically based on the chosen format.

You can modify the filename with the --filename option:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --filename=customers
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --filename=employees

Alternatively, specify the filename in config/packages/doctrine_diagram.yaml:

doctrine_diagram:
    er:
        filename: '%kernel.project_dir%/customers'
    class:
        filename: '%kernel.project_dir%/employees'

Tip

You don't need to set a filename extension; it is automatically added according to the selected diagram format.

docs.title: Set diagram size
docs.text:
You can generate diagrams in different sizes:

  • mini: Display only table or class names.
  • midi: Include tables and columns for Entity-Relationship diagrams and classes and properties for Class diagrams.
  • maxi: Show table names, columns, and views for Entity-Relationship diagrams. And classes, properties, and methods for Class diagrams.

Adjust the diagram size using the --size option:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --size=mini
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --size=midi

Alternatively, set the size in the config file:

doctrine_diagram:
    er:
        size: mini
    class:
        size: midi

docs.title: Customizing themes
docs.text:
Use themes to change the look of your diagrams.

From the terminal, you can set the theme using --theme option.

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --theme=sandstone
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --theme=crt-amber

Alternatively, set the theme in the config file:

doctrine_diagram:
    er:
        theme: sandstone
    class:
        theme: crt-amber

This is a complete list of available themes:

Please note that all themes might not be available in your system since themes are dependent of the version of PlantUML you have installed.

sandstone theme:

crt-amber theme:

docs.title: Filtering tables and classes
docs.text:
You can customize the elements appearing in a diagram using --include and --exclude options.

To select specific elements to appear (tables from the ER diagram and classes from Class diagram), use the --include option. On the other hand use the --exclude option to remove elements.

Internally, these two filters are applied in order, first the --include option and then the --exclude option is used on the tables specified by the --include option. When the --include options is omitted, all the tables in the database are going to be used.

Entity-relationship diagram examples:

# Display three tables in the diagram
bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --include=table1 --include=table2 --include=table3

# Hide 'secrets' table
bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --exclude=secrets

Class diagram examples:

# Print all entities but remove 'App\Entity\CreditCard' from the diagram
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --exclude=App\\Entity\\CreditCard

Tip

Note how, in the terminal, we had to escape the backslash character.

Explicitly typing the elements one by one, can be extremely long. This is where wildcards are very useful:

  • Use the ? wildcard to represent a single character.
  • Use the * wildcard to represent multiple characters.

Entity-relationship diagram examples:

# Display only accounting tables from years 20XX 
bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --include=accounting_20??

# Remove all tables starting with 'classified'
bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --exclude=classified*

Class diagram examples:

# Only use entities from Acme and App namespaces
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --include=Acme\\* --include=App\\*

# Remove all entities from Lexik vendor
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --exclude=Lexik\\Bundle\\*

In the config file, use the include and exclude in the same way.

doctrine_diagram:
    er:
        include:
            - user_*
            - exams_20??
        exclude:
            - user_passwords
            - user_secrets
    class:
        include:
            - App\Entity\*
            - Lexik\*
        exclude:
            - App\Entity\CreditCard

Tip

Remember, when you omit the include key, all the tables/classes are used.

docs.title: Change the diagram format
docs.text:
Three formats are supported: png, svg, and puml.

You can set the format from the terminal using the --format option:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --format=puml
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --format=puml

Alternatively, you can set the format in config/packages/doctrine_diagram.yaml:

doctrine_diagram:
    convert:
        format: svg

Tip

If you encounter difficulties generating your diagram, use the puml format as it doesn't require PlantUML.

docs.title: Specifying how to convert PlantUML diagrams
docs.text:
Internally, DoctrineDiagramBundle will always generate diagrams in puml format first. If the requested format is puml, then the diagram will be returned as is. Otherwise, if the requested format is png or svg, you will need to configure a "converter".

PlantUML can be used with two kind of converters:

  1. As a local plantuml.jar file.
  2. As a remote PlantUML server.

Use the following options to use a jar file to convert diagrams.

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --converter=jar --jar=/usr/share/plantuml/plantuml.jar

doctrine_diagram:
    convert:
        converter: jar
        jar: /usr/share/plantuml/plantuml.jar

The other alternative to generate images is to use a remote PlantUML server:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --converter=server --server=http://localhost:8080/plantuml

doctrine_diagram:
    convert:
        converter: server
        server: http://localhost:8080/plantuml

The default and recommended setting is auto. DoctrineDiagramBundle checks for a locally available PlantUML installation first, then falls back to the configured server. If you install PlantUML with the jawira/plantuml Composer package, auto mode detects its plantuml.jar automatically; you do not need to set the jar path. See PlantUML setup for installation instructions.

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --converter=auto

doctrine_diagram:
    convert:
        converter: auto

Please read the dedicated page about how to install PlantUML.

docs.title: Dev project
docs.text:
Add this to composer.json in your project to use the local copy of Diagram Bundle.

{
  "repositories": [{"type": "path", "url": "../doctrine-diagram-bundle"}]
}

Change minimum-stability:

{
  "minimum-stability": "dev"
}

Set branch name:

{
  "jawira/doctrine-diagram-bundle": "dev-theme"
}

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
To build documentation material theme is required.

pip install mkdocs-material
phing mkdocs:serve

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
DoctrineDiagramBundle requires PHP 8.2 or later, Symfony 7 or 8, Doctrine Bundle 2.5 or later in the 2.x series or 3.x, and Doctrine ORM 2.9 or later in the 2.x series or 3.x. Composer installs the required dependencies with the bundle.

PlantUML is needed only when you want diagrams in svg or png format. You can install it locally or use a PlantUML server; see PlantUML setup. The puml format does not require PlantUML.

docs.title: Install with Symfony Flex
docs.text:
In your project directory, allow community-contributed Symfony recipes if you have not already enabled them:

composer config extra.symfony.allow-contrib true

Then install the bundle as a development dependency:

composer require jawira/doctrine-diagram-bundle --dev

Symfony Flex installs the bundle recipe, which registers the bundle for the dev and test environments. Review the recipe changes in your project.

docs.title: Install without Symfony Flex
docs.text:
Install the bundle with Composer:

composer require jawira/doctrine-diagram-bundle --dev

Register the bundle in config/bundles.php:

<?php

return [
    // ...
    Jawira\DoctrineDiagramBundle\DoctrineDiagramBundle::class => ['dev' => true, 'test' => true],
];

docs.title: Incompatible versions
docs.text:
PlantUML implemented some changes in class diagrams, as a consequence DoctrineDiagramBundle displays the following error:

Failed to open stream: HTTP request failed! HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

The following versions are incompatible with DoctrineDiagramBundle.

  • PlantUML v1.2026.7
  • PlantUML v1.2026.8

The issue is reported for PlantUML v1.2026.7 and v1.2026.8. Check the issue links below for updates and use a different PlantUML version if affected.

By default, the bundle uses the public PlantUML server, whose version can change independently of your application. Configure a local installation or a custom server to control the PlantUML version.

A workaround to this problem is to use a different version of PlantUML server, learn how to do this in PlantUML setup. Then follow instructions in Configure the bundle to specify which PlantUML version to use.

You can find more details about the issue in:

  • https://github.com/jawira/doctrine-diagram-bundle/issues/87
  • https://github.com/jawira/doctrine-diagram-bundle/issues/88

docs.title: Error: "Failed to open stream: HTTP request failed!"
docs.text:
This error occurs when you are trying to generate a diagram in SVG or PNG formats, and you are using the public PlantUML server.

The problem is that the diagram you are trying to create is too large, and the PlantUML server has limited diagram sizes to avoid abuse.

Solution 1

Use PlantUML locally instead of a web server. This is explained in Configuration page.

Solution 2

Generate a diagram in PUML format. This diagram is generated locally and doesn't require the PlantUML server. Then, use the plantuml executable locally to convert the PUML diagram to the desired format.

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --format=puml
bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --format=puml

Solution 3

Do not use the public PlantUML server; use your own PlantUML server instead.

Then, access your server using the command option --server, or in the doctrine_diagram.yaml file.

docs.title: Error 'Unknown column type "uuid" requested'
docs.text:
You encounter the following error when trying to generate a diagram:

CRITICAL [console] Error thrown while running command "doctrine:diagram". Message: "Unknown column type "uuid" requested. Any Doctrine type that you use has to be registered with \Doctrine\DBAL\Types\Type::addType ().

To fix this error, add a custom type in the doctrine.yaml config file. For example:

doctrine:
    dbal:
        types:
            uuid: Symfony\Bridge\Doctrine\Types\UuidType

Source: Registering custom Mapping Types.

docs.title: Error "Syntax Error"
docs.text:
When trying to generate a diagram, you get the following error in the terminal:

Error Output:
================
ERROR
7
Syntax Error?
Some diagram description contains errors

Solution

Use a newer version of PlantUML, older versions of PlantUML do not support features like themes and custom namespace separators.

docs.title: PlantUML setup
docs.text:
PlantUML is required to save diagrams in png or svg format. By default, DoctrineDiagramBundle will use the public PlantUML web server: https://www.plantuml.com/plantuml/ to generate those images.

DoctrineDiagramBundle can use either a locally installed version of PlantUML or connect to a remote PlantUML server.

This bundle requires a relatively recent version of PlantUML; versions newer than v1.2022.0 are recommended. Check the Known issues page for version-specific compatibility notes.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
To work properly, PlantUML has the following requirements:

  • java 8
  • GraphViz - Installing GraphViz

Please follow the official documentation to learn how to install PlantUML in your OS: https://plantuml.com/en/starting

docs.title: Installing PlantUML with Composer
docs.text:
I have developed a convenience package to install PlantUML using Composer.

https://packagist.org/packages/jawira/plantuml

composer require jawira/plantuml

You will find plantuml.jar inside vendor directory: ./vendor/jawira/plantuml/bin/plantuml.jar.

docs.title: PlantUML server
docs.text: A PlantUML server is required if you want to save diagrams in png and svg formats.

docs.title: PlantUML server with Docker
docs.text:
An alternative method to set up a PlantUML server involves leveraging Docker.

Use Docker to establish a PlantUML server using the following command. This command ensures that the server is accessible via port 8080.

docker run -d -p 8080:8080 plantuml/plantuml-server:jetty

The PlantUML server endpoint includes the /plantuml path. Set it in doctrine_diagram.yaml as shown below.

# config/packages/doctrine_diagram.yaml
doctrine_diagram:
    # ...
    convert:
        server: 'http://localhost:8080/plantuml'

For further details, refer to: PlantUML in Docker Hub

docs.title: Running PlantUML picoserver
docs.text:
First, ensure you have PlantUML installed on your system. Then run following command to create a local PlantUML server available on port 8080:

plantuml -picoserver:8080

Once executed, your server becomes accessible through http://localhost:8080. Additionally, declare this new server in config/packages/doctrine_diagram.yaml as follows:

# config/packages/doctrine_diagram.yaml
doctrine_diagram:
    # ...
    convert:
        server: 'http://localhost:8080/plantuml'

For more information visit: PlantUML Picoweb Documentation

docs.title: Generating diagrams
docs.text:
DoctrineDiagramBundle provides two Symfony commands to generate diagrams from your database:

  • doctrine:diagram:er - To generate Entity-Relationship diagrams.
  • doctrine:diagram:class - To generate Class diagrams.

docs.title: Generating Entity-Relationship diagrams
docs.text:
An Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram visually represents the entities (such as tables) in a database, their attributes (such as columns), and the relationships between them.

Use the following command to generate Entity-Relationship diagrams:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er

You can also use the following shortcut:

bin/console d:d:er

If you are using the default configuration, a file named er.svg will be created at the root of your project.

If your application uses multiple databases, you can specify which DBAL connection to use using the --connection option:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --connection=employees

You can also set the DBAL connection in doctrine_diagram.yaml. See configuration for the available command options and configuration file settings.

doctrine_diagram:
    er:
        connection: employees

Set connection to null, and the default connection will be used.

docs.title: Generating Class diagrams
docs.text:
A UML Class diagram visually represents the Doctrine Entities in your project, including their properties, methods, and the relationships between them.

Use the following command to generate Class diagrams:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:class

You can also use the following shortcut:

bin/console d:d:class

Info

DoctrineDiagramBundle will only use Doctrine entities to generate the diagram. Additionally, only properties with the ORM\Column attribute are displayed, other class properties are ignored.

If you are using the default configuration, a file named class.svg will be created at the root of your project.

If your application uses multiple databases, you can specify which Entity Manager to use using the --em option:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:class --em=customers

In doctrine_diagram.yaml:

doctrine_diagram:
    class:
        em: customers

Set em to null, and the default Entity Manager will be used.

docs.title: How to pipe output
docs.text:
Use php://stdout as the destination file to redirect image to standard output.

For example:

bin/console doctrine:diagram:er --filename="php://stdout" --format=puml | tee diagram.puml
